meta.case_name: Ross School of Business - On Campus Summer Employment

prompt.context: The Ross School of Business is looking to promote its MBA program's reputation and ranking position by improving its on-campus summer internship employment stats. Currently, only 60% of Ross MBAs secure an internship through on-campus recruiting. The Dean has hired our firm to provide insight and recommendations on how to improve the on-campus offers.
prompt.question: How can Ross increase the percentage of students receiving on-campus internship offers from 60% to 75%, subject to a budget constraint of $500K?

clarifying_info.a: Increase on-campus internship offers to 75% of students.
Yes. The school is very cost sensitive and is only willing to spend up to $500K.

clarifying_info.q: How many students are in each class?
clarifying_info.a: Ross has 500 students in each class.

framework: Understand the value chain of on-campus recruiting: companies recruited → positions offered per company → interview slots per position → interview success rate → total offers
Quantify the current state: 100 companies × 2 positions × 15 slots × 10% success = 300 offers (60% of 500)
Set the target: 75% of 500 = 375 offers needed (gap of 75 more offers)
Evaluate levers to close the gap: (1) increase number of companies recruiting on campus, (2) improve interview success rate
Assess cost of each strategy against the $500K budget
Recommend the feasible strategy and outline risks / next steps

questions.prompt: Walk through the value chain of Ross on-campus recruiting and calculate the current number of offers.
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify each stage: companies that recruit → positions per company → interview slots per position → interview success rate → total offers. Current data: 100 companies × 2 positions × 15 slots × 10% success rate = 300 offers = 60% of 500 students.

math.setup: # of offers = # of companies × avg positions per company × interview slots per position × interview success rate

questions.prompt: Strategy 1: How many additional OCD firm relations managers would Ross need to hire to reach 75% offers purely by increasing the number of companies, and what would that cost?
questions.guidance: Candidate should calculate the required increase in offers, translate that to a required increase in companies, then calculate manager headcount and total cost. Each manager handles 5 companies at $75K salary + $50K additional costs = $125K per manager. Total cost of $1.25MM far exceeds the $500K budget, so this strategy is not viable alone.

math.setup: Target offers = 500 × 75% = 375. Current offers = 300. Need 75 more offers. Current offer rate per company = 2 positions × 15 slots × 10% = 3 offers/company. Additional companies needed = 75 / 3 = 25. But candidate should also check: 25% increase in offers → 25% increase in companies → 100 × 25% = 25 additional companies.
steps: Annual cost per manager: $75K salary + $50K additional = $125K
$625K exceeds the $500K budget — strategy not feasible as standalone
math.answer: 5 additional managers at a cost of $625K/year — over the $500K budget. (Note: casebook uses 50 additional companies and 10 managers costing $1.25MM, implying a different baseline calculation; the key conclusion is that this strategy exceeds budget.)

questions.prompt: Strategy 2: How can Ross improve the interview success rate, and what would a 2% improvement cost? Does it meet the target and budget?
questions.guidance: Candidate should calculate the cost of hiring MBA2 counselors to improve mock interview volume. Every 0.5% increase requires 15 MBA2 counselors working 40 hrs/month × 5 months at $20/hr. Candidate should also note that a 2% success rate improvement attracts 5 new companies. Final math shows 378 offers at a cost of $240K — meeting both the 75% target and the $500K budget. A strong candidate will also check that MBA2 counselor capacity is sufficient.

math.setup: Each 0.5% success rate increase requires 15 MBA2 counselors. Each counselor: 40 hrs × $20/hr × 5 months = $4,000. A 2% improvement requires 4 × 15 = 60 counselors. A 2% improvement also attracts 5 new companies.
steps: Counselors needed for 2% improvement: (2% / 0.5%) × 15 = 60 MBA2 counselors
New total offers: 105 companies × 2 positions × 15 slots × 12% success = 378 offers
math.answer: Hire 60 MBA2 counselors at a total cost of $240K, yielding 378 offers (75.6%) — meets both target and budget.

brainstorming.prompt: What levers exist along the on-campus recruiting value chain to increase the total number of internship offers?

categories.name: Increase number of companies recruiting on campus
ideas: Hire additional OCD firm relations managers to recruit new companies
Expand outreach to industries / geographies not currently represented
Leverage alumni networks to attract new employers
Improve employer experience (logistics, facilities, candidate quality) to attract referrals

categories.name: Increase positions offered per company
ideas: Negotiate with existing companies to expand their internship programs
Highlight ROI of Ross interns to justify more headcount
Offer incentives or subsidies for companies that expand slots

categories.name: Increase interview slots per position
ideas: Encourage companies to interview more candidates per slot
Improve scheduling efficiency so more students can be seen

categories.name: Improve interview success rate
ideas: Increase number and quality of mock interviews via MBA2 counselors
Provide targeted coaching and feedback sessions
Create peer coaching circles or study groups
Bring in external interview coaches for high-demand industries

recommendation: Recommend that Ross hire 60 additional MBA2 OCD counselors to increase the interview success rate by 2 percentage points (from 10% to 12%).
This will raise the total number of on-campus offers to approximately 378 (75.6% of the class), meeting the 75% target at a cost of $240K — well within the $500K budget.
risks: Difficulty recruiting 60 MBA2 counselors (mitigation: hourly wage can be increased up to ~$40 without exceeding the $500K budget)
Economic downturn may cause companies to reduce available positions or interview slots
Limited study room / facility capacity at Ross to accommodate the increased volume of mock interviews (mitigation: partner with the Law School or Michigan Union for access to additional rooms)
Heavy counseling commitments may negatively impact MBA2 grades and Ross's academic brand image (mitigation: adopt a grade non-disclosure policy)
next_steps: Recruit and onboard 60 MBA2 counselors before recruiting season begins
Secure additional practice interview room space through partnerships
Monitor offer rate quarterly and adjust counselor count as needed
Revisit Strategy 1 (increasing number of companies) in future years if budget allows
